text:
Maria: Observed a regression after the kernel-selector rollout: p95 CPU on hosts handling many tiny requests went up ~20%. Collecting notes here.
Aj: Confirmed. Flamegraphs: heavy stacks in request_normalize() -> tokenizer::init() and http2_writev_small(). Link: http://perf.red/fg/5987659999
Ben: KV cache hit-rate for short prefixes also dropped (baseline ~95% -> 86%). Looks like normalization moved before tokenization and changes hash keys.
Devon: Which change reordered normalization? Aj's PR last night?
Aj: Yea, PR#4128. I moved normalization earlier to help kernel selection pick a dense kernel for batched sequences. Didn't expect this to affect tiny single-frame requests.
Maria: Repro steps: replay 200k 32-64 byte prompts -> token.init dominates CPU and we emit many tiny frames (http2 write count spikes).
Ben: Hypothesis: early normalization changes canonicalization of whitespace -> less KVC hits; also token init repeated for every request.
Aj: Quick mitigation ideas: 1) for payloads < 128 bytes, defer normalization until after tokenize(); 2) enable writev coalesce for http2 proxy for frames < 256 bytes; 3) pool tokenizer objects to avoid re-init cost.
Devon: Also add a kernel-selector hint: prefer the "tiny-seq" kernel for seq_len <= 16 so selector doesn't thrash.
Ben: I ran a local canary: normalization-after-tokenize + tokenizer-pool reduces host CPU ~14%, kvcache hit back to ~91%, writev coalesce cuts small TCP writes by ~35%.
Maria: Sounds promising. We should be cautious: that normalization reorder could affect model inputs for some edge customers. Need a compatibility test and a flag guarded rollout.
Aj: Proposed canary patch (sketch):
```
if payload.len < 128 and http2.frames == 1:
  set_fast_path(FAST_PARSE_DEFER_NORMALIZE)
  token = tokenizer_pool.checkout()
  tokens = token.tokenize(payload)
  normalize_post(tokens)
else:
  normalize_pre(payload)
```
I'll instrument kvcache.hit, token.init.latency, and http2.writev.count.
InfraBot: deploy-bot: starting canary deploy canary-5987 -> 3 hosts.
Devon: Add a metric: kernel_selector.chosen_by_hint and kernel_selector.swap_count to detect thrash.
Ben: One more observation: when selector flips kernels due to prebatch hints, we see cold caches on GPU memory mappings and kv-key churn. Favor stable kernel if flips exceed threshold.
Maria: Action items: Aj - push canary + telemetry; Ben - run distributed sim across small, medium, large models; Devon - RFC for ingress grouping rule and kernel-stability guard; Maria - prepare short incident note + testing checklist.
Aj: ETA: canary in ~2h, early metrics in 12-24h. Will post flamegraphs to the canary channel.
Maria: Thanks. Please mark any customers impacted and add rollback plan.
Devon: Filing the RFC now.
Ben: Will share sim results once finished.
Aj: will follow up with logs.
Maria: :thumbsup:
